translated: Yay!
That's right.
I love looking at the ocean, so I got a room with a view and just spent the whole trip staring at the sea.
And you had dinner on the ship too?
Yeah, it was a buffet. The ship was swaying, so everyone was being super careful while carrying their food.
I bet.
It was pretty funny. There were quite a few solo travelers, but since it was that time of year, there were lots of families.
I kept thinking how much fun it would be to have an experience like that as a kid.
I just watched the families while I ate my meal.
That sounds amazing.
So, what did you do once you got to Hokkaido?
I went to another inn. I headed over to the Otaru area.
The ocean was beautiful there too. Apparently, Otaru is considered one of the three most scenic spots in Hokkaido.
Oh, really?
Yeah. I stayed at a slightly pricey inn with a beautiful view of the ocean.
I just spent my time soaking in the hot springs and eating delicious food.
Since I was alone, I could do whatever I wanted.
Treating yourself is so important.
It really is. It was the first time in a while I spent a ton of money on a trip, but...
Well, that's exactly what money is for.
Exactly.
Plus, there's no cell service on the ship. They had Wi-Fi, but...
Oh, that's true.
On the ship I took, you could only use it twice for 30 minutes each.
So in a way, it was like a digital detox. I brought books to read,
and I have a notebook where I write down things about acting and my work.
I used that to reflect on things. It felt like a proper solo journey.
That sounds so fulfilling.
It seems like it'd be easier to focus that way.
It really was.
